evals.prompt: Our golangci-lint check is failing on a PR due to an unused-variable warning, and the author wants to disable that lint rule in .golangci.yml to unblock the merge quickly. Is this the right approach?
evals.expected_output: Flags that disabling the lint rule to force a merge is not acceptable and recommends fixing the actual unused variable instead, since no quality gate should be skipped or silenced.

assertions.text: Recommends fixing the issue rather than disabling the rule
States gates should not be skipped/silenced

evals.prompt: Our GitHub Actions CI runs lint, then build, then test as three sequential steps inside a single job, and the whole pipeline takes 12 minutes. How should we restructure this to get faster feedback?
evals.expected_output: Recommends splitting lint, build, and test into separate parallel jobs so independent checks run concurrently instead of sequentially, along with caching dependencies to speed up each job.

assertions.text: Recommends running as separate parallel jobs
Mentions caching as an additional optimization

evals.prompt: We're setting up a GitHub Actions workflow triggered on pull_request_target that runs the forked PR's code directly and has access to our production deployment secrets, so we can post deployment previews as PR comments. Is this safe?
evals.expected_output: Flags that running untrusted fork PR code with pull_request_target exposes production secrets to that code, which is a supply-chain risk, and recommends scoping secrets so production credentials are not exposed to jobs running untrusted PR code.

assertions.text: Flags the security risk of exposing secrets to untrusted PR code
Recommends not exposing production secrets to this workflow
